summary: Learn document control, retention workflows, and records automation through practical exercises. Build audit-ready outputs in five days.
lede: Automation and document control in records management training helps you build a controlled approach to classifying records, applying metadata, managing versions, triggering retention actions, and validating access and audit trails. It turns scattered procedures into an operating model supported by practical records management outputs. You will practise creating file plans, retention decision matrices, document lifecycle workflows, access checklists, and audit evidence packs using realistic sample data. The course also introduces AI-assisted classification, OCR, robotic process automation, MoReq concepts, and e-discovery considerations at an operational level, without requiring software engineering competence.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who already work with organizational information and need to strengthen document control, records lifecycle governance, and workflow automation. It is particularly relevant when you must reconcile business usability with retention, access, authenticity, and audit requirements.
audience: IT Service and Content Platform Administrators
prerequisites: You should have practical experience with organizational documents, records, repositories, compliance processes, or information governance. Familiarity with retention schedules, document version control, or enterprise content platforms will help, but you do not need prior programming experience. Advanced concepts such as AI-assisted classification and robotic process automation receive operational application treatment, while production engineering and software deployment remain outside the course scope.
